parts.label: Part 2
parts.article:
Part 2.

You will hear a talk about a new waterfront development. 1st, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.

Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16.

Well, thank you all for coming along to this talk about our new waterfront development. The council has developed the old boat harbor to provide a new area of leisure facilities right here on the city's waterfront, and we want to encourage local people to visit the new development.

Okay, I'll start with some background. Long before the harbor was built, the 1st building on the site was put up by Sir Michael Grayson. He'd been working in Asia for a time, and when he came home, he began developing the city along this part of the coast. However, there was a problem with the site. Because the land was low-lying, whenever there was a storm, large waves would break on the shore, which could be destructive. So Grayson built a wall along the beach to protect the land behind it, and that solved the problem.

Then, in 1915, the land here became more valuable. Some companies were not doing very well financially, so the government wanted to increase local business activity, and they did this by constructing a better road connecting this site to the city center. That had an important impact, and later on, over the following years, it led to additional migration to this part of the country.

One obvious change came in the 1920s when the 1st boat harbor was built here. The water was too shallow for large ocean liners carrying people, so these continued to use the main wharf further south.

But the smaller boats that went out each day to catch snapper, tuna, and other species to feed the city started to use this as their port.

Defense Force ships, of course, already had their own base further up the coast.

Then, in the 1930s, warehouses were built around the harbor, and it was made deeper. That's because international trade was increasing. It's true that some parts of the economy, like sheep farming, were in decline, but forestry was a major growth sector.

The timber was brought here by train, kept in the new buildings, then shipped to foreign countries.

So, why do we need this latest redevelopment? Well, over the years, the harbor had become run-down. They talked about doing something for 10 years before anything actually happened. Finally, the project started when a team of designers began work and a consultation plan was drawn up. And now, 14 years after the project started, the new waterfront area is open to the public. We hope that nothing will need to be done now for another 25 years when the harbor wall will need upgrading.

I have to say, some parts of the redevelopment were quite difficult. We were lucky with the steamship because it had already been restored. What we really wanted were some traditional trams, so we bought some from another city. But it turned out to be a long process, and they needed a lot of modification for our system, the hardest thing we had to do.

We decided against renovating the old bridge and instead replaced it with a modern one, which was very simple in comparison.

Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.

Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.

Okay, so now I'll just tell you about a few of the features of the new development. Um, so if you look at your maps, you'll see we're here, where it says South Gate, near the bottom of the map. So 1st, the playground. From South Gate, walk north until you come to the lifting bridge. Cross the bridge to the area we call North Wharf, and the playground is at the eastern end there, right beside the water.

So, the open-air cinema. They show movies on a big outdoor screen, after dark, of course. It's a lot of fun. And it's up on North Wharf. Look in the northwest corner. It's a circular enclosure. You can't miss it.

Now, we've also built a small aquarium that's full of local species of fish. It's close to South Gate. Find Pier One, and it's right down at the end of that.

Now, the Maritime Museum is well worth a visit. It's the only one of its sort in the country.

From South Gate, you go... Well, actually, you can go 2 ways. Either go around the boat harbor or go over the lifting bridge, and it's the long, thin building that runs right along the north side of the boat harbor.

Okay, well, that's the end of my talk, but if you have any-

That is the end of Part 2. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 2.

questions.question: What problem did Sir Michael Grayson have with the original site?

analyses.content: 录音明确指出，以前一遇到风暴，大浪拍岸就会产生破坏性（destructive），这与选项B（海水造成破坏）完美对应。
你可能听到“shore”或“beach”就过度联想去选A（沙质土地），或者主观猜测C（水污染），但录音并没有提到这两个信息，做题时千万不要脑补。

However, there was a problem with the site. Because the land was low-lying, whenever there was a storm, large waves would break on the shore, which could be destructive. So Grayson built a wall along the beach to protect the land behind it, and that solved the problem.

options.option: more people moved to the area.
options.optionContent: more people moved to the area.

questions.question: In 1915, the land in this area became more valuable because

analyses.content: 录音中提到政府为了增加商业活动，修建了一条连接该地与市中心的更好道路（constructing a better road），这直接对应选项A（交通路线改善）。
你可能会听到“migration”而误选B，但人口迁入是修路几年后带来的“结果”，并不是1915年土地升值的“原因”；同时录音只说个别公司财务不佳，并未提及国家经济快速扩张，排除C。

Then, in 1915, the land here became more valuable. Some companies were not doing very well financially, so the government wanted to increase local business activity, and they did this by constructing a better road connecting this site to the city center. That had an important impact, and later on, over the following years, it led to additional migration to this part of the country.

questions.question: The first boat harbour was built in the 1920s for

analyses.content: 录音明确说明，每天出海捕捉鲷鱼、金枪鱼等来供应城市的小船开始使用这里作为港口，直接对应选项C（渔业）。
你可能会在录音中听到“carrying people”（客船）和“Defense Force”（军队）从而在A和B中纠结，但录音已明确表明水太浅不适合客船（排除B），且军队有自己专属的基地（排除A），干扰信息的排除要果断。

One obvious change came in the 1920s when the 1st boat harbor was built here. The water was too shallow for large ocean liners carrying people, so these continued to use the main wharf further south. But the smaller boats that went out each day to catch snapper, tuna, and other species to feed the city started to use this as their port. Defense Force ships, of course, already had their own base further up the coast.

options.option: to store wool for sale locally
options.optionContent: to store wool for sale locally

questions.question: Why were warehouses built in the 1930s?

analyses.content: 录音指出林业是增长部门，木材（timber）被保存在新建筑里然后运往国外（shipped to foreign countries），对应选项A（为了出口储存木材）。
你可能听到“international trade”就想当然选了B（进口），或者听到“sheep farming”联想到羊毛选了C，但录音明确说木材是运往国外（出口），且牧羊业正处于衰退中，不要抓错核心词。

Then, in the 1930s, warehouses were built around the harbor, and it was made deeper. That's because international trade was increasing. It's true that some parts of the economy, like sheep farming, were in decline, but forestry was a major growth sector. The timber was brought here by train, kept in the new buildings, then shipped to foreign countries.

questions.question: How long after the start of the project was the new waterfront area opened?

analyses.content: 录音中清晰且直接地说出“项目开始后的14年（14 years after the project started），新的滨水区向公众开放”，直接锁定B选项。
你可能会听到10年或25年被带偏，但10年是项目实施前大家空谈的时间，25年是未来不需要重新维修的预期时间，读题时必须牢牢盯住“开放前花费的时间”这一核心提问。

So, why do we need this latest redevelopment? Well, over the years, the harbor had become run-down. They talked about doing something for 10 years before anything actually happened. Finally, the project started when a team of designers began work and a consultation plan was drawn up. And now, 14 years after the project started, the new waterfront area is open to the public. We hope that nothing will need to be done now for another 25 years when the harbor wall will need upgrading.

questions.question: The hardest part of the redevelopment involved

analyses.content: 录音点明，传统有轨电车（traditional trams）需要进行大量改造才能适应现有系统，这是“我们必须做的最困难的事情（the hardest thing we had to do）”，对应选项C。
你可能会因为听到了“steamship”或“old bridge”而动摇，但录音表示蒸汽船已经修复好了属于“幸运”（排除B），旧桥直接换新桥“非常简单”（排除A），注意听形容词和题目“hardest”的对应。

I have to say, some parts of the redevelopment were quite difficult. We were lucky with the steamship because it had already been restored. What we really wanted were some traditional trams, so we bought some from another city. But it turned out to be a long process, and they needed a lot of modification for our system, the hardest thing we had to do. We decided against renovating the old bridge and instead replaced it with a modern one, which was very simple in comparison.
从南门向北走过升降桥（lifting bridge）到North Wharf后，游乐场位于该区域的“东端”（eastern end）且“紧挨着水”（beside the water），在地图上完美对应C的位置。
你可能会在听到过桥后没有迅速找到参照物，务必抓牢“eastern end”和“beside the water”这两个定向词，避免错选成同样在North Wharf区域的A。

So 1st, the playground. From South Gate, walk north until you come to the lifting bridge. Cross the bridge to the area we call North Wharf, and the playground is at the eastern end there, right beside the water.
录音不仅说了在North Wharf，还给出了极度具体的方位“西北角（northwest corner）”和外观特征“圆形场地（circular enclosure）”，一眼就能锁定A。
你可能只听到了“North Wharf”的大概区域，如果跟丢了方位词，请注意利用录音中给出的形状特征（circular）在图上直接找对应。

So, the open-air cinema. They show movies on a big outdoor screen, after dark, of course. It's a lot of fun. And it's up on North Wharf. Look in the northwest corner. It's a circular enclosure. You can't miss it.
录音提示离南门很近，关键参照物是“Pier One（1号码头）”，水族馆就在它的尽头（at the end of that），对应图上的G。
你可能听到“close to South Gate”后没有继续跟进具体参照物，容易在F、H、I等位置盲猜，做地图题一定要紧跟明确的地标名称（Pier One）。
Now, we've also built a small aquarium that's full of local species of fish. It's close to South Gate. Find Pier One, and it's right down at the end of that.
录音中无论提示哪种走法，最终的物理定位都是沿着船港北侧（north side of the boat harbor）的那栋“长条形建筑（long, thin building）”，直接对应B。
你可能会被前面复杂的绕路或过桥路线（2 ways）绕晕而跟丢，此时要直接听取目的地本身的空间特征（长、窄、船港北侧）进行一击必中。

Now, the Maritime Museum is well worth a visit. It's the only one of its sort in the country. From South Gate, you go... Well, actually, you can go 2 ways. Either go around the boat harbor or go over the lifting bridge, and it's the long, thin building that runs right along the north side of the boat harbor.
